column3: according to a broad definition that is commonly accepted
column4: “reuse” refers to the use of public data by third parties for purposes other than the public service mission for which the data was produced or received (this definition has been recalled here : (https://www.data.gouv.fr/fr/posts/nos-reflexions-sur-les-reutilisations-des-donnees-ouvertes/).

column1: This definition stems from the Code of Relations between the Public and the Administration : “Public information contained in documents communicated or published by the administrations mentioned in the first paragraph of article L. 300-2 may be used by any person who wishes to do so for purposes other than those of the public service mission for which the documents were produced or received.” (https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/codes/article_lc/LEGIARTI000033219044). This definition is similar to the PSI Directive definition : “Public sector bodies collect
column2: produce
column3: reproduce and disseminate documents in order to fulfil their public service mission. The use of these documents for other purposes constitutes re-use.”

column1: The complexity and the need to clarify the definition of reuse has been emphasised in the literature
column2: particularly with respect to research data
column3: a key issue being the distinction between use and reuse.

column2: more restrictive approaches have also emerged : some consider that only perennial uses of data are reuses while others consider any use of data as reuse.

column1: In our day to day operations
column2: any exploitation of data in order to obtain information is considered as reuse
column3: whether this exploitation is freely accessible or not : following that definition
